$comment: Phase 32A. Quotes for every grazingRestrictions value on herbicide, insecticide and fungicide plugins, keyed pluginId → fact path (grazeDays, hayDays, lactatingDairyGrazeDays, meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays, notForPasture, manureCarryover, speciesExceptions.<speciesId>[.lactating].grazeDays|hayDays). Each entry is { url, publisher, date, quote, note? } read from the product label. `pastureAllowlist` lists pasture-labelled products that have no grazingRestrictions yet, each with a reason. The gate in apps/web/src/lib/plugins/sourceCoverage.gate.test.ts fails on a pasture-labelled product that is neither covered nor listed, and on a listed product that is no longer a gap.

grazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: There are no restrictions on grazing or grass hay harvest intervals following application of Chaparral at labeled rates. However, cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds will reduce weed control. Wait 14 days after herbicide application to cut grass hay to allow herbicide to work.

hayDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: There are no restrictions on grazing or grass hay harvest intervals following application of Chaparral at labeled rates. However, cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds will reduce weed control. Wait 14 days after herbicide application to cut grass hay to allow herbicide to work.
hayDays.note: The label sets no hay interval; the 14 days is advice for weed control. Recorded as 14 (stricter reading) rather than 0.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: There are no restrictions on grazing or grass hay harvest intervals following application of Chaparral at labeled rates. However, cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds will reduce weed control. Wait 14 days after herbicide application to cut grass hay to allow herbicide to work.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: The label names no separate interval for lactating dairy animals and its no-restriction grazing statement has no dairy exception, so 0.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: There are no restrictions on grazing or grass hay harvest intervals following application of Chaparral at labeled rates. However, cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds will reduce weed control. Wait 14 days after herbicide application to cut grass hay to allow herbicide to work.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: The label states no slaughter withdrawal anywhere and says there are no grazing interval restrictions, so 0. The grazing statement is the only support; no sentence says 'no slaughter restriction'.

manureCarryover.quote: Do not plant a broadleaf crop in fields treated in the previous year with manure from animals that have grazed forage or eaten hay harvested from treated areas until an adequately sensitive field bioassay is conducted to determine that the aminopyralid concentration in the soil is at level that is not injurious to the crop to be planted.

carryoverManureWindow.quote: Do not use manure from animals that have grazed forage or eaten hay harvested from treated areas within the previous 3 days, in compost, mulch, or mushroom spawn.
carryoverManureWindow.note: Quote only for the 3-day figure. The label also says: 'This product is persistent and may be present in treated plant materials for months to years after application.' and 'Do not sell or transport treated plant materials or manure from animals that have grazed on treated plant materials off-site for compost distribution or for use as animal bedding/feed for 18 months after application.' Also: 'Do not transfer grazing animals from areas treated with Chaparral to areas where sensitive broadleaf crops occur without first allowing 3 days of grazing on an untreated pasture. Otherwise, urine and manure may contain enough aminopyralid to cause injury to sensitive broadleaf plants.'; and a broadleaf crop may not be planted in fields treated with such manure 'until an adequately sensitive field bioassay is conducted to determine that the aminopyralid concentration in the soil is at level that is not injurious to the crop to be planted.' A registrant bulletin giving a longer or different window was not read; none is recorded.

carryoverHayOffFarm.quote: Hay can only be used on the farm or ranch where product is applied.
carryoverHayOffFarm.note: Also: 'Do not use grasses treated with Chaparral in the preceding 18 months for hay intended for export outside the United States.' and, off-site: 'Do not sell or transport treated plant materials or manure from animals that have grazed on treated plant materials off-site for compost distribution or for use as animal bedding/feed for 18 months after application.'

carryoverCompostWarning.quote: Do not use treated plant residues , including hay or straw from areas treated within the preceding 18 months, in compost, mulch, or mushroom spawn.
carryoverCompostWarning.note: Also: 'Do not use hay or straw from areas treated with Chaparral within the preceding 18 months or manure from animals feeding on hay treated with Chaparral in compost.' The label points to EPA's aminopyralid compost-contamination page. The space before the comma in the quote is as extracted from the PDF.

manureCarryoverDays.note: Copied verbatim from the carryoverManureWindow entry for chaparral-aminopyralid-metsulfuron (Phase 33C ruling M-17).

hayOffFarmRestricted.note: Copied verbatim from the carryoverHayOffFarm entry for chaparral-aminopyralid-metsulfuron (Phase 33C ruling M-17).

grazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: Except for lactating dairy animals, there are no grazing restrictions following application of this product.

hayDays.note: Same 14 days in the Rangeland and Permanent Pastures section: 'Do not cut forage for hay within 14 days of application.' The label also says the product may not be applied to forage that is to be cut and sold for commercial purposes.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: The label gives no day count. Recorded as 365 days, the stricter reading of 'until the next growing season'.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Slaughter Restrictions: During the season of application, withdraw livestock from grazing treated grass at least 3 days before slaughter.

manureCarryover.quote: Animals that have been fed triclopyr treated forage must be fed forage free of triclopyr for at least 3 days before movement to an area where manure may be collected, or sensitive crops are grown.
manureCarryover.note: The label also bars selling or moving treated plant material, or manure from animals that grazed it, off-site for compost or bedding/feed for 30 days after application.

hayDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)

manureCarryover.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
manureCarryover.quote: Do not spread manure from animals that have grazed or consumed forage or hay from treated areas on land used for growing susceptible broadleaf plants or apply such materials to land used for growing broadleaf crops, ornamentals, orchards, or other susceptible desirable plants.
manureCarryover.note: Also: 'Do not transfer livestock from treated grazing areas (or feeding of treated hay) to sensitive broadleaf crop areas without first allowing 7 days of grazing on an untreated pasture (or feeding of treated hay).' and no use of hay, straw, manure or bedding straw from treated areas for composting or mulching where susceptible plants may be grown the following season.

carryoverManureWindow.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
carryoverManureWindow.quote: Do not transfer livestock from treated grazing areas (or feeding of treated hay) to sensitive broadleaf crop areas without first allowing 7 days of grazing on an untreated pasture (or feeding of treated hay). If livestock are transferred within less than 7 days of grazing untreated pasture or eating untreated hay, urine and manure may contain enough clopyralid to cause injury to sensitive broadleaf plants.
carryoverManureWindow.note: The label gives a 7-day livestock transfer wait, not a window for how long manure stays hazardous; it states no manure-hazard duration. Plant-residue wording: 'To promote herbicidal decomposition, plant residues should be evenly incorporated or burned.' A registrant bulletin giving a longer or different window was not read; none is recorded.

carryoverHayOffFarm.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
carryoverHayOffFarm.quote: Do not use hay or straw from treated areas for composting or mulching on susceptible broadleaf crops.
carryoverHayOffFarm.note: No limit on moving, selling or distributing treated hay off the farm was found in the label text; the nearest statements concern composting and mulching (turnip use, with a pointer to 'Residues in Plants or Manure'). Peppermint and spearmint: 'Do not feed spent peppermint and spearmint hay slugs to livestock.'

carryoverCompostWarning.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
carryoverCompostWarning.quote: Do not use plant residues, including hay or straw from treated areas, or manure or bedding straw from animals that have grazed or consumed forage from treated areas, for composting or mulching where susceptible plants may be grown the following season.
carryoverCompostWarning.note: Also: 'Do not spread manure from animals that have grazed or consumed forage or hay from treated areas on land used for growing susceptible broadleaf plants or apply such materials to land used for growing broadleaf crops, ornamentals, orchards, or other susceptible desirable plants.'

manureCarryoverDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
manureCarryoverDays.quote: Do not transfer livestock from treated grazing areas (or feeding of treated hay) to sensitive broadleaf crop areas without first allowing 7 days of grazing on an untreated pasture (or feeding of treated hay). If livestock are transferred within less than 7 days of grazing untreated pasture or eating untreated hay, urine and manure may contain enough clopyralid to cause injury to sensitive broadleaf plants.
manureCarryoverDays.note: Copied verbatim from the carryoverManureWindow entry for stinger (Phase 33C ruling M-17).

carryoverManureWindow.publisher: Corteva Agriscience / Dow AgroSciences (EPA PPLS stamped label, GF-4556 alternate brand ResiCore REV)
carryoverManureWindow.quote: Do not graze or harvest rotational cover crops for food or animal feed for 18 months following the last application of GF-4556.
carryoverManureWindow.note: The label text (EPA registration notice dated 7/25/22, label GF-4556) has no manure, urine, compost, mulch or off-farm hay statement; the nearest livestock-feed statement is the quoted cover-crop rule.

carryoverManureWindow.quote: Do not graze or feed forage, hay, or straw from treated areas to livestock.
